learning_objectives: Understand how AI creates fake content
outline: How AI can generate realistic fake content
Risks of deepfake audio, video, and images
Importance of source verification and media literacy

slides.title: Misinformation and Deepfakes
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on Misinformation and Deepfakes.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to understand how **AI** creates fake content.
You will also identify the risks of deepfake media.
Furthermore, you will learn to verify sources.
You will also recognize the impact of misinformation.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration:
You will need a device with internet access.
No specific software is required for this tutorial.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
A basic understanding of what **AI** is will be helpful.
No prior technical knowledge is needed.

slides.title: AI and Fake Content
slides.narration:
Can **AI** create things that are not real?
Yes, **AI** can generate very convincing fake content.
This includes fake audio, video, and images.
**AI** learns patterns from vast amounts of data.

slides.title: Deepfake Technology
slides.narration:
This technology is often called **deepfake**.
Think of it like an artist who learns to paint.
The artist can then create new, realistic paintings.
**AI** does this with faces, voices, and actions.

slides.title: Risks of Deepfakes
slides.narration:
What are the dangers of such fake content?
Deepfakes can spread false information very quickly.
They can make someone appear to say or do anything.
This can harm reputations and cause confusion.

slides.title: Audio and Video Risks
slides.narration:
Imagine a fake video of a politician.
It shows them saying something they never said.
This can influence public opinion wrongly.
You saw the impact.
Now reflect on this.

slides.title: Real-World Impact
slides.narration:
Have deepfakes caused real problems?
Yes, deepfakes have been used in many hoaxes.
They have targeted public figures and common people.
This technology can even impact elections.

slides.title: Societal Consequences
slides.narration:
For example, a deepfake audio could mimic a CEO's voice.
It could then trick employees into transferring money.
This shows the financial and social dangers.
Now we learn how to protect ourselves.

slides.title: Verifying Sources
slides.narration:
How can we tell if content is real or fake?
Always question the source of information.
Check if the content comes from a trusted channel.
Look for official websites or news outlets.

slides.title: Media Literacy
slides.narration:
This skill is called media literacy.
It helps us critically evaluate what we see.
Look for inconsistencies in lighting or sound.
Unusual facial expressions can be a sign.

slides.title: Critical Thinking
slides.narration:
Does the story sound too good or too bad to be true?
Pause and think before you share anything.
Cross-check facts with multiple reliable sources.
This helps us fight the spread of misinformation.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, we understood how **AI** creates deepfakes.
We identified the risks of misinformation.
We learned the importance of source verification.
We also discussed media literacy skills.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Find a news article reporting a deepfake incident.
Analyze how the deepfake was detected.
Write a short paragraph on its impact.
Share your findings with a friend.
